maya.activity: Wake beside Daniel, stretch quietly, read the news on my phone, and get dressed while watching his face for signs that he feels worse.
maya.intention: Start the day gently and notice whether Daniel needs extra help.

maya.activity: Make coffee and a quick breakfast, pack my lunch, and prepare ginger-like lemon tea for Daniel. Carry his mug to him and bring my breakfast to the kitchen counter.
maya.intention: Feed us both without asking Daniel to manage breakfast, and leave him something soothing.

maya.activity: Rinse the breakfast dishes, put my lunch into its container, gather my work things, and leave for the department.
maya.intention: Get out on time while keeping the kitchen and entry clear for our relative.
Travel calmly and arrive prepared for the workday.

maya.activity: Work at the transportation department, review Wednesday site-visit materials, and respond to planning messages.
maya.intention: Keep the workday focused while leaving enough attention for home later.

maya.activity: Eat the lunch I packed and check my phone for messages from home.
maya.intention: Take a real break and make sure Daniel is managing comfortably.

maya.activity: Continue department work and complete site-visit follow-up notes before packing up.
maya.intention: Finish cleanly so the evening does not become another unfinished task.

maya.activity: Commute home, keeping an eye on messages and the weather for the walk.
maya.intention: Return with enough time to check on Daniel and help with hosting.

maya.activity: Change into comfortable clothes, put my work blouse and trousers away, set my laptop in the left desk drawer, and make tea for Daniel.
maya.intention: Separate work from home and make the first minutes of the evening easier for him.

maya.activity: Take a brisk but shorter neighborhood walk, then return home and check quietly whether Daniel or our relative needs anything.
maya.intention: Clear my head without staying away from home too long.

maya.activity: Prepare a simple dinner, carry plates and water to the dining table, and eat with Daniel and our relative while keeping the conversation easy.
maya.intention: Feed everyone and help the visit feel warm without demanding much from Daniel.

maya.activity: Clear the dinner dishes, store leftovers, rinse the saucepan, and wipe the stovetop and counter.
maya.intention: Reset the shared surfaces before settling in for the evening.

maya.activity: Sit with our relative in the living room for a low-key visit, keep the lights comfortable, and bring Daniel water if he settles on the sectional.
maya.intention: Be present as a host while quietly monitoring Daniel's comfort.

maya.activity: Say goodnight to our relative, choose clothes for tomorrow, read fiction quietly, and put my phone on charge.
maya.intention: Make room for a calm bedtime routine despite the unusual household rhythm.

maya.activity: Settle into bed beside Daniel, keep water within his reach, and turn out the light.
maya.intention: End the day attentive but not intrusive, and get enough rest for tomorrow.

daniel.activity: Wake slowly, take my temperature, shower, and make tea instead of coffee while listening briefly to a quiet podcast. I will move carefully and leave the tea mug on the bathroom counter only while I finish getting ready, then carry it to the kitchen.
daniel.intention: Check how I feel and start the morning gently without forcing my usual routine.

daniel.activity: Make a small, mild breakfast and eat with Maya before she leaves, keeping conversation easy and letting her know I will work more slowly today. I will carry the mug and bowl to the kitchen counter and leave the tasting spoon on the sink side.
daniel.intention: Eat something and coordinate the day without making my illness or the visit feel dramatic.

daniel.activity: Settle at the queen bed work setup, open the work laptop, and handle only the essential morning production call and urgent dialogue notes. I will keep the laptop cable and mouse close at hand and write down priorities rather than trusting my foggy memory.
daniel.intention: Protect the important work while limiting cognitive strain.

daniel.activity: Stop work, drink water, and lie down on the queen bed with the room quiet and the laptop left on the lower shelf. I will set the notebook beside it so I do not have to search for my notes later.
daniel.intention: Rest before symptoms and fatigue build up.

daniel.activity: Make a simple broth-based lunch preparation in the kitchen, using canned tomatoes, garlic, and pasta or rice. I will carry the saucepan and wooden spoon to the stovetop and set tasting spoons on the sink side as usual.
daniel.intention: Prepare nourishing food early so I do not have to cook when more tired.

daniel.activity: Eat a small portion standing at the kitchen counter, drink water, and put the saucepan and bowl near the sink rather than attempting a full cleanup.
daniel.intention: Get food down and conserve energy for rest and essential work.

daniel.activity: Return to the guest room for light dialogue editing and monitoring, taking frequent pauses whenever the words or waveform stop making sense. I will make a short written list of anything that can wait until tomorrow.
daniel.intention: Complete a reduced amount of focused work without pretending I am fully well.

daniel.activity: Rest with the lights low, check my temperature again, and drink tea. I will leave the mug on the nightstand and keep the phone nearby in case Maya or the relative needs to reach me.
daniel.intention: Recover before the afternoon and avoid spreading my limited energy across too many tasks.

daniel.activity: Do a brief administrative pass on the laptop, answer only necessary messages, and update the priority list. I will stop rather than attempt a remote studio session if concentration slips.
daniel.intention: Keep work from accumulating while respecting the illness.

daniel.activity: Carry a clean towel and spare pillow into the queen bedroom if the guest setup needs anything, then sit or lie down and rest. I will straighten only the most visible surface and leave the rest alone.
daniel.intention: Make the visiting relative comfortable without turning hosting into a project.

daniel.activity: Make another cup of tea and sit quietly in the living room. If Maya’s relative is there, I will greet them warmly, offer tea or water, and listen more than I talk; I will avoid piano practice and any loud audio.
daniel.intention: Be present and welcoming while keeping the atmosphere calm.

daniel.activity: Rest on the sectional and check messages only briefly. I will leave my phone on the bar cart, where it will probably remain until someone calls, and keep the remote work laptop in the guest room rather than dragging it into the living room.
daniel.intention: Have genuine downtime before the evening meal and avoid starting another task.

daniel.activity: Warm the broth and prepare a very simple dinner contribution, helping only as much as my energy allows. I will carry the saucepan to the stovetop, use a tasting spoon on the sink side, and sit down if standing makes me light-headed.
daniel.intention: Support Maya’s dinner routine without assuming I can host or cook a full meal.

daniel.activity: Eat a small dinner at the dining table with Maya and her relative if I feel steady enough, keeping conversation easy and making a light joke if I apologize for being slow. I will carry my bowl and mug to the counter afterward.
daniel.intention: Share some normal social time while allowing myself to leave early if exhausted.

daniel.activity: Clear only the most visible dishes and kitchen surface, then return to the sectional with tea. I will offer the relative water once, check whether Maya needs anything, and avoid hovering.
daniel.intention: Reduce the obvious clutter and settle into a quiet evening.

daniel.activity: Wash up, brush my teeth, change into sleepwear, and take my temperature once more. I will put the used towel in the laundry basket and leave the thermometer where I can find it in the morning.
daniel.intention: Finish the day’s care routine without adding unnecessary tasks.

daniel.activity: Carry water and a mug of tea to the king bed, keep the lights and conversation low, and rest beside Maya while the relative settles in the guest room. I will set the phone on the nightstand and go to sleep rather than trying to work again.
daniel.intention: Get the earliest practical rest and end the day feeling cared for rather than behind.
